title: Governed commit absorbs content it did not admit

preconditions: two writers share one canonical worktree and one index
writer-a resolves and admits a bundle of paths
writer-b mutates the index or the worktree before writer-a's commit executes
faultFingerprint.observation: the resulting commit tree is not equal to the bundle writer-a admitted

variants.summary: A path no admitted slice declared appears in the candidate tree.
An admitted path keeps its name but its content is replaced between admission and assembly.
variants.expectedInvariant: committed blob equals the sealed blob
variants.expectedOutcome: the sealed content is committed; the substitution never lands

variants.summary: No task-scoped bundle resolves and the executor would commit whatever the shared index holds.
variants.expectedInvariant: no governed commit without a sealed bundle

variants.summary: A shared-delivery plan is rejected after the commit object was written and the ref advanced.
variants.expectedInvariant: a rejected plan leaves HEAD unchanged
variants.expectedOutcome: no commit object is published and HEAD is byte-identical

variants.summary: A staged deletion has no index entry, so a seal built only from present content omits it and the file survives the commit.
variants.expectedInvariant: deletion is sealed as an explicit tombstone and the committed tree omits the path
variants.expectedOutcome: the deletion and any accompanying modification both land

variants.summary: A tombstoned path is still present in the candidate tree.
variants.expectedInvariant: a tombstone requires absence from the committed tree

variants.summary: A deletion outside the admitted scope is staged alongside an admitted one.
variants.expectedInvariant: unadmitted removals are excluded, never absorbed
variants.expectedOutcome: excluded from the candidate; forcing it in fails closed

variants.summary: Two writers seal their own slices from the one shared index at overlapping times.
variants.expectedInvariant: a prepared seal is stable while the other writer stages
variants.expectedOutcome: both seals carry only their own paths and each candidate tree proves independently

variants.summary: A governed commit reaches candidate assembly with no admitted bundle and no named seal route.
variants.expectedInvariant: sealing the live shared index is a named decision, never a default
variants.expectedOutcome: fail-closed before a candidate index exists

variants.summary: An overlay re-declares an admitted path with identical content under a different provenance.
variants.expectedInvariant: supersession is allowed only for paths the transaction declares it staged
variants.expectedOutcome: fail-closed before any ref update, with the conflict named

variants.summary: Another lane advances HEAD between admission and ref update.
variants.expectedInvariant: ref update is compare-and-swap, never a force
variants.expectedOutcome: the other lane's commit survives and the delivery requeues

notes: Writer identities, paths and timestamps in this fixture are synthetic. The family reproduces from the shape of the interleaving, not from any recorded task, actor or date.
